pairs.fullEnglish: At the beginning, יְיָ created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was desolate and empty, and darkness spread over the face of the deep; and a wind from before יְיָ was blowing over the face of the waters.

qualifications.he: התרגום אומר כאן שרוח מלפני יְיָ נושבת על פני המים.
qualifications.en: The Targum speaks here of a wind from before יְיָ blowing over the waters.

pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light.
יְיָ saw that the light was good, and יְיָ separated the light from the darkness.
יְיָ called the light Day, and He called the darkness Night. There was evening and there was morning: one day.
יְיָ said, ‘Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it separate water from water.’
יְיָ made the expanse and separated the water below the expanse from the water above the expanse; and it was so.
יְיָ called the expanse Heavens. There was evening and there was morning: a second day.
יְיָ said, ‘Let the water beneath the heavens gather into one place, and let the dry land appear’; and it was so.
יְיָ called the dry land Earth, and the gathering place of the waters He called Seas. יְיָ saw that it was good.
יְיָ said, ‘Let the earth put forth vegetation: plants whose seed is sown, and fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kinds, with their seed in them, upon the earth’; and it was so.
The earth brought forth vegetation: plants whose seed is sown, according to their kinds, and trees bearing fruit with their seed in it, according to their kinds. יְיָ saw that it was good.
There was evening and there was morning: a third day.
יְיָ said, ‘Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate day from night; let them be for signs and appointed times, and for counting days and years by them.
Let them be lights in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth’; and it was so.
יְיָ made the two great lights: the greater light to rule by day, the smaller light to rule by night, and the stars.
יְיָ set them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
to rule by day and by night, and to separate light from darkness. יְיָ saw that it was good.
There was evening and there was morning: a fourth day.
יְיָ said, ‘Let the waters teem with a teeming multitude of living creatures, and let birds fly over the earth, across the face of the expanse of the heavens.’
יְיָ created the great sea creatures, every living moving creature with which the waters teemed, according to their kinds, and every flying bird according to its kind. יְיָ saw that it was good.
יְיָ blessed them, saying, ‘Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the water in the seas; and let birds multiply on the earth.’
There was evening and there was morning: a fifth day.
יְיָ said, ‘Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, creeping creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kinds’; and it was so.
יְיָ made the wild animals of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and every creeping creature of the earth according to its kind. יְיָ saw that it was good.

יְיָ said, ‘Let Us make a human in Our image, according to Our likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the livestock, the whole earth, and every creeping creature that creeps upon the earth.’
יְיָ created the human in His image; in the image of יְיָ He created him; male and female He created them.

יְיָ blessed them, and יְיָ said to them, ‘Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and exercise power over it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, and every living creature that moves upon the earth.’
יְיָ said, ‘See, I have given you every plant whose seed is sown upon the face of the whole earth, and every tree that has tree fruit whose seed is sown: it shall be yours for food.
And to every wild animal of the earth, every bird of the heavens, and everything that moves upon the earth in which there is living life, [I have given] all green plants for food’; and it was so.

qualifications.he: המילים שבסוגריים באנגלית משלימות את הפועל מן הפסוק הקודם.
qualifications.en: The bracketed English supplies the governing verb from the preceding verse.

pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very well ordered. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.
The heavens and the earth, and all their hosts, were completed.
On the seventh day יְיָ finished the work that He had done, and on the seventh day He rested from all the work that He had done.
יְיָ blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work that יְיָ created to do.
These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day when יְיָ אֱלֹהִים made earth and heavens.
No tree of the field was yet on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprouted, because יְיָ אֱלֹהִים had not brought rain down upon the earth, and there was no human to cultivate the ground.
A cloud would rise from the earth and water the whole face of the ground.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים created the human, dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and it became in the human a speaking spirit.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים planted a garden in Eden beforehand, and placed there the human whom He had created.

qualifications.he: כאן מִלְּקַדְמִין מתורגם במשמעות זמן: מקודם. בפסוק ג:כד ההקשר הוא מקום, מזרח הגן.
qualifications.en: Here מִלְּקַדְמִין is rendered temporally, ‘beforehand.’ In 3:24 the context instead concerns position, east of the garden.

pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ אֱלֹהִים caused to grow from the earth every tree that is desirable to see and good to eat, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree by eating whose fruit people become discerning between good and evil.

qualifications.he: התרגום מפרש את שם העץ באמצעות השפעת אכילת פריו.
qualifications.en: The Targum explains the tree by the effect of eating its fruit.

pairs.fullEnglish: A river would go out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it would divide and become four riverheads.
The name of one is Pishon; it surrounds the whole land of Chavilah, where the gold is.
The gold of that land is good; there are bdellium and burla stones.

qualifications.he: זהותה המדויקת של האבן בוּרְלָא אינה מוכרעת כאן.
qualifications.en: The exact gemstone denoted by burla is uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: The name of the second river is Gichon; it surrounds the whole land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Diglas; it flows to the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים took the human and settled him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate it and to guard it.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים commanded the human, saying, ‘From every tree of the garden you may freely eat.
But from the tree by eating whose fruit people become discerning between good and evil, you shall not eat, for on the day you eat from it you shall surely die.’
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים said, ‘It is not fitting for the human to be by himself. I will make him a support corresponding to him.’

יְיָ אֱלֹהִים created from the earth every wild animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and brought [each] to the human to see what he would call it; whatever the human called each living creature was its name.
The human gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the heavens, and to every wild animal of the field; but for the human he did not find a support corresponding to him.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים cast sleep upon the human, and he slept; He took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים built the rib that He had taken from the human into a woman, and brought her to the human.
The human said, ‘This time, [she is] bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. This one shall be called Woman, because this one was taken from her husband.’

qualifications.he: התרגום משתמש בבעלא, בעל, ולא רק במילה כללית לאיש.
qualifications.en: The Targum uses בעלא, ‘husband,’ rather than merely a generic word for a man.

pairs.fullEnglish: Therefore a man shall leave the bedchamber of his father and his mother, and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
The two of them were naked, the human and his wife, and they were not ashamed.
The serpent was cleverer than every wild animal of the field that יְיָ אֱלֹהִים had made. It said to the woman, ‘Is it really so that יְיָ said, “You shall not eat from any tree of the garden”?’
The woman said to the serpent, ‘We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden.
But of the fruit of the tree in the midst of the garden, יְיָ said, “You shall not eat from it, nor touch it, lest you die.”’
The serpent said to the woman, ‘You shall certainly not die.
For it is revealed before יְיָ that on the day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like great ones, discerning between good and evil.’

The woman saw that the tree was good to eat, that it was healing for the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to look at. She took of its fruit and ate; she also gave to her husband with her, and he ate.

qualifications.he: אַסֵּי מתורגם כאן כמרפא לעיניים; משמעותו המדויקת במשפט אינה מוכרעת.
qualifications.en: אַסֵּי is rendered here as ‘healing for the eyes’; its precise force in this clause is uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: The eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. They stitched together fig leaves for themselves and made themselves girdles.
They heard the voice of the Word of יְיָ אֱלֹהִים moving in the garden toward the cooling of the day; and the human and his wife hid from before יְיָ אֱלֹהִים among the trees of the garden.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים called to the human and said to him, ‘Where are you?’
He said, ‘I heard the voice of Your Word in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid.’
He said, ‘Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree concerning which I commanded you not to eat from it?’
The human said, ‘The woman whom You gave to be with me—she gave me from the tree, and I ate.’
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים said to the woman, ‘What is this that you have done?’ The woman said, ‘The serpent led me astray, and I ate.’

יְיָ אֱלֹהִים said to the serpent, ‘Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all livestock and more than every wild animal of the field. On your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.

I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your children and her children. He will remember against you what you did to him at the beginning, and you will lie in wait for him at the end.’

qualifications.he: התרגום מתאר זכירת הפגיעה הקדומה והמתנה לפגיעה בסוף; אין זה נוסח מילולי של ראש ועקב.
qualifications.en: The Targum describes remembering the former injury and lying in wait at the end; it does not literally reproduce the Hebrew’s head-and-heel wording.

pairs.fullEnglish: To the woman He said, ‘I will greatly increase your pains and your pregnancies; in pain you shall bear children. Your desire shall be toward your husband, and he shall rule over you.’

To the human He said, ‘Because you listened to the word of your wife and ate from the tree concerning which I commanded you, saying, “You shall not eat from it,” the ground is cursed because of you. Through toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.
It shall grow thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the earth from which you were created; for you are dust, and to dust you shall return.’
The human called his wife’s name Chavah, because she was the mother of all human beings.
יְיָ אֱלֹהִים made for the human and his wife garments of honor upon the skin of their flesh, and clothed them.

יְיָ אֱלֹהִים said, ‘Behold, the human has become unique in the world, knowing good and evil of himself; and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat and live forever—’

qualifications.he: מִנֵּהּ נקשר כאן לידיעת האדם מעצמו. המשפט האחרון נשאר מותנה, והפעולה בפסוק הבא היא שילוחו מן הגן.
qualifications.en: מִנֵּהּ is taken here with the human’s knowing ‘of himself.’ The final clause remains a ‘lest’ construction, followed in the next verse by his expulsion from the garden.

pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ אֱלֹהִים sent him from the Garden of Eden to cultivate the ground from which he was created.
He drove out the human, and stationed to the east of the Garden of Eden the cherubs and the sharp edge of the revolving sword, to guard the way to the tree of life.
The human knew Chavah his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain. She said, ‘I have acquired a man (from) before יְיָ.’

qualifications.he: מִן נתונה בסוגריים, ולכן יש כאן שתי קריאות: מלפני יְיָ, או לפני יְיָ בלי מִן.
qualifications.en: מִן (“from”) is parenthesized, allowing two readings: “from before יְיָ,” or “before יְיָ” without “from.”

pairs.fullEnglish: She continued to give birth to his brother, Hevel. Hevel was a shepherd of sheep, and Cain was a cultivator of the earth.
At the end of a period of days, Cain brought some of the produce of the earth as an offering before יְיָ.
Hevel too brought some of the firstborn of his sheep and of their fat portions; and there was favor from before יְיָ toward Hevel and his offering.
But toward Cain and his offering there was no favor. Cain became exceedingly angry, and his face fell.
יְיָ said to Cain, ‘Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?

Is it not so that, if you improve your deeds, you will be forgiven? But if you do not improve your deeds, your sin is kept for the day of judgment, when payment will be exacted from you if you do not repent. And if you repent, you will be forgiven.’

qualifications.he: הפירעון מותנה באי־תשובה; התרגום מוסיף במפורש שאם ישוב ייסלח לו.
qualifications.en: The punishment is conditional on not repenting; the Targum expressly adds that if he repents he will be forgiven.

pairs.fullEnglish: Cain spoke to Hevel his brother; and when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Hevel his brother and killed him.
יְיָ said to Cain, ‘Where is Hevel your brother?’ He said, ‘I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?’
He said, ‘What have you done? The voice of the blood of the descendants who were destined to come from your brother is crying out before Me from the earth.
And now you are cursed from the ground, which opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you cultivate the ground, it will no longer give you its strength. You shall be a wanderer and an exile on the earth.’
Cain said before יְיָ, ‘My guilt is too great to be forgiven.
See, You have driven me today from the face of the earth, and it is impossible to hide from before You. I shall be a wanderer and an exile on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.’
יְיָ said to him, ‘Therefore, whoever kills Cain—retribution will be exacted from him at seven generations.’ יְיָ placed a sign upon Cain so that whoever found him would not kill him.

qualifications.he: מושא הכינוי מִנֵּהּ, ממנו, אינו ודאי. בפסוק כד נאמר במפורש ששבעה דורות ניתנו לקין; אין כאן זיהוי ודאי של הכינוי עם הורג עתידי.
qualifications.en: The referent of מִנֵּהּ (“from him”) is uncertain. Verse 24 expressly says that seven generations were granted to Cain; the pronoun does not unambiguously identify a future killer.

pairs.fullEnglish: Cain went out from before יְיָ and dwelt in the land as an exile and a wanderer, as had been decreed for him, east of the Garden of Eden.
Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Chanoch. He was building a city, and he called the city’s name after the name of his son, Chanoch.
To Chanoch was born Irad; Irad fathered Mechuyael; Mechiyael fathered Mesushael; and Mesushael fathered Lemech.
Lemech took two wives for himself: the name of one was Adah, and the name of the second was Tzillah.
Adah bore Yaval; he was the master of those who dwell in tents and own livestock.
His brother’s name was Yuval; he was the master of everyone who plays upon the mouth of the nevel, those skilled in the music of the lyre and the pipe.

qualifications.he: זהותו המדויקת של הכלי נבלא והיחס בינו לכנורא אינם מוכרעים.
qualifications.en: The exact instrument denoted by nevel and its relation to the following lyre are uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: Tzillah too bore Tuval Cain, the master of all those skilled in working copper and iron. Tuval Cain’s sister was Naamah.

Lemech said to his wives, ‘Adah and Tzillah, hear my voice! Wives of Lemech, listen to my words! I have not killed a man on whose account I should bear guilt, nor have I injured a youth on whose account my descendants should perish.

qualifications.he: בדברי למך כאן יש שלילה מפורשת של הריגת איש ושל פגיעה בנער.
qualifications.en: Lemech’s words here expressly deny killing a man and injuring a youth.

pairs.fullEnglish: For seven generations were granted to Cain; shall not seventy-seven [be granted] to Lemech his descendant?’
The human again knew his wife, and she bore a son and called his name Shais, for she said, ‘יְיָ has given me another son in place of Hevel, whom Cain killed.’
To Shais too a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. Then, in his days, human beings ceased praying in the name of יְיָ.

qualifications.he: חָלוּ מִלְּצַלָּאָה מתורגם כאן כחדילה מתפילה, ולא כהתחלת תפילה.
qualifications.en: חָלוּ מִלְּצַלָּאָה is rendered here as ceasing to pray, not beginning to pray.

pairs.fullEnglish: This is the book of the generations of Adam. On the day יְיָ created the human, He made him in the likeness of אֱלֹהִים.
Male and female He created them; He blessed them and called their name Adam on the day they were created.
Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered [a son] in his likeness, resembling him, and called his name Shais.
After he fathered Shais, Adam’s days were eight hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
Shais lived one hundred and five years and fathered Enosh.
After he fathered Enosh, Shais lived eight hundred and seven years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Shais were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
Enosh lived ninety years and fathered Kainan.
After he fathered Kainan, Enosh lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
Kainan lived seventy years and fathered Mahalalel.
After he fathered Mahalalel, Kainan lived eight hundred and forty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Kainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
Mahalalel lived sixty-five years and fathered Yered.
After he fathered Yered, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.
Yered lived one hundred and sixty-two years and fathered Chanoch.
After he fathered Chanoch, Yered lived eight hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Yered were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
Chanoch lived sixty-five years and fathered Mesushalach.
After he fathered Mesushalach, Chanoch walked in the fear of יְיָ for three hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Chanoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
Chanoch walked in the fear of יְיָ, and he was no longer, for יְיָ put him to death (variant: did not put him to death).

qualifications.he: בלי לָא משמעות המשפט היא שיְיָ המית את חנוך; עם לָא שבסוגריים משמעותו היא שלא המיתו. שתי הקריאות נשארות אפשריות.
qualifications.en: Without לָא, the clause says that יְיָ put Chanoch to death; with the parenthesized לָא, it says that He did not put him to death. Both readings remain possible.

pairs.fullEnglish: Mesushalach lived one hundred and eighty-seven years and fathered Lemech.
After he fathered Lemech, Mesushalach lived seven hundred and eighty-two years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Mesushalach were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.
Lemech lived one hundred and eighty-two years and fathered a son.
He called his name Noach, saying, ‘This one will comfort us from our work and from the weariness of our hands, from the earth that יְיָ has cursed.’
After he fathered Noach, Lemech lived five hundred and ninety-five years, and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Lemech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died.
Noach was five hundred years old, and Noach fathered Shaim, Cham, and Yafes.
When human beings began to multiply upon the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
the sons of the great ones saw that the daughters of human beings were beautiful; and they took wives for themselves from whomever they desired.

יְיָ said, ‘This evil generation shall not endure before Me forever, because they are flesh and their deeds are evil. I have granted them a reprieve of one hundred and twenty years, if they will repent.’

qualifications.he: מאה ועשרים השנים הן ארכת זמן הקשורה לתשובה, ולא קביעה כללית שתוחלת חייו של כל אדם היא מאה ועשרים שנה.
qualifications.en: The one hundred and twenty years are a reprieve linked to repentance, not a general statement that every human lifespan is one hundred and twenty years.

pairs.fullEnglish: Mighty men were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of the great ones would go in to the daughters of human beings and they bore [children] to them. Those were the mighty men of old, men of renown.
יְיָ saw that human wickedness had become great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all day.
יְיָ reconsidered in His Word that He had made human beings on the earth; and He said in His Word that He would break their power according to His will.

qualifications.he: בְּמֵימְרֵהּ, במאמרו, מסייג את לשון השיבה. אין בכך קביעה של שינוי בידיעה האלוהית או של תחושה גופנית.
qualifications.en: “In His Word” qualifies the reconsideration. This is not a statement of a change in Divine knowledge or of bodily emotion.

pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ said, ‘I will wipe away the human beings whom I created from the face of the earth, from human beings to livestock, to creeping creatures and to the birds of the heavens; for I have reconsidered in My Word that I made them.’
But Noach found mercy before יְיָ.

Thus said יְיָ, God of the world, יְיָ, who created the heavens and suspended them, who completed the earth and its inhabitants, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk upon it:
‘I am יְיָ; I have raised you in truth, strengthened your hand, and established you. I will give you as a covenant of a people, as a light of the nations,

to open the eyes of the house of Israel, who are as though blind to the Torah; to bring their exiles out from among the nations, where they are like prisoners; and to redeem them from the subjection of kingdoms, where they are afflicted like prisoners in darkness.

qualifications.he: נַלְוַתְהוֹן מובנת כאן לפי ההקשר כגולים שלהם; צורת המילה החריגה משאירה ספק בקריאה זו.
qualifications.en: נַלְוַתְהוֹן is understood here from context as ‘their exiles’; the unusual form leaves this reading uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: I am יְיָ; that is My name. The glory with which I revealed Myself to you I will not give to another people, nor My praise to those who worship images.
The former things—behold, they have come; and new things I declare. Before they come I will announce them to you.’
Sing a new praise before יְיָ; declare His praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea and all that fills it, the islands and those who inhabit them.
The proverbs of Shlomo, son of David, king of Israel:
to know wisdom and discipline, to understand sayings of discernment;
to receive the discipline of understanding, and righteousness, judgment, and uprightness;
to give prudence to the inexperienced, and knowledge and thought to the young.
Let the wise person hear and increase knowledge, and let the discerning person acquire guidance,
to understand a proverb and a wondrous saying, the words of the wise and their riddles.

qualifications.he: פִלְאֲתָא מתורגמת כאן כאמרה מופלאה; היחס המדויק לחידה או למליצה אינו מוכרע.
qualifications.en: פִלְאֲתָא is rendered here as “a wondrous saying”; its exact relation to a riddle or figurative saying is uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: Let the wilderness and the towns that are inhabited in it give praise; let those who dwell in the Arabian desert rejoice. The dead shall give praise when they come out of their eternal resting places; from the tops of the mountains they shall raise their voices.

qualifications.he: התרגום מזכיר במפורש מתים היוצאים מבתי עולמם, מעבר לנוסח הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: The Targum expressly includes the dead coming out of their eternal resting places, an expansion beyond the Hebrew verse.

pairs.fullEnglish: They shall ascribe glory before יְיָ, and declare His praise in the islands.
יְיָ has revealed Himself to perform mighty deeds; to perform might He reveals Himself in anger. With an utterance, also with trembling, He reveals Himself against His enemies in His might.

qualifications.he: מִלוּל וזִיעַ מתורגמים כאן כאמירה ורעד. היחס התחבירי ביניהם ובין התגלות הגבורה אינו מוכרע.
qualifications.en: מִלוּל and זִיעַ are rendered as an utterance and trembling. Their syntactic relation to the revelation of might is uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘I have given them a reprieve from long ago, so that they might return to the Torah, but they did not return. Like birth pangs upon a woman giving birth, My judgment shall be revealed upon them; they shall become desolate and perish together.

qualifications.he: ארכת הזמן ניתנה לשם חזרה לתורה, והעונש המתואר בא לאחר שלא חזרו.
qualifications.en: The reprieve was given so that they might return to the Torah; the punishment described follows their failure to return.

pairs.fullEnglish: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of ייָ; fools scorn wisdom and discipline.
Hear, my son, the discipline of your father, and do not stray from the teaching of your mother,
for they are beauty and grace for your head, and a necklace for your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.
I will lay waste mountains and heights, and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn rivers into islands and dry up pools.

I will lead the house of Israel, who are like the blind, on a way they did not know; on paths they have not learned I will guide them. I will turn darkness before them into light and rough ground into a level place. These things I will do for them, and I will not cast them far away.
Those who worship images, who say to a cast image, “You are our gods,” shall turn backward and be utterly ashamed.
You wicked people, who are like the deaf—do you not have ears? Hear! And you guilty people, who are like the blind—do you not have eyes? Look and see!

Is it not so that, if the wicked repent, they will be called My servants, and [so will] the guilty [to whom] I sent My prophets? But the wicked are destined to receive the punishment of their sins; yet if they repent, they will be called the servants of יְיָ.

qualifications.he: הכינוי עבדים תלוי בתשובה. המילים שבסוגריים באנגלית משלימות את הקישור התחבירי לחייבים שנשלחו אליהם נביאים; הקישור אינו מפורש ואין זה ציווי חדש.
qualifications.en: Being called servants is conditional upon repentance. The bracketed English supplies the syntactic link to the guilty to whom prophets were sent; that link is not explicit, and the clause is not a new imperative.

pairs.fullEnglish: If they say, ‘Come with us; let us lie in wait for blood; let us hide to ambush the innocent without cause.

qualifications.he: הפסוק מתחיל תנאי: אם יאמרו. דברי הפיתוי נמשכים עד פסוק יד, והאזהרה לבן באה בפסוק טו.
qualifications.en: The verse begins a condition, ‘If they say.’ The enticement continues through verse 14; the warning to the son follows in verse 15.

pairs.fullEnglish: Let us swallow them alive like the grave, and those without blemish like those who go down to the pit.
We shall find every kind of wealth and precious thing; we shall fill our houses with plunder.
Cast your lot among us; there shall be one purse for all of us’—
my son, do not go on the way with them; hold back your foot from their paths.
You have seen many things, but have not kept [them]. Your ears have been opened, but you have not received instruction.

qualifications.he: מושא השמירה אינו מפורש במילה זו; הוא הושלם באנגלית בסוגריים מתוך המשפט.
qualifications.en: The object of ‘kept’ is not explicit in this clause and is supplied in English brackets from the sentence.

pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ desires to grant Israel merit; He will exalt those who carry out His Torah and will strengthen them.

But it is a people plundered and oppressed. All the young men are covered with shame, and in houses of imprisonment they are afflicted. They have become spoil, with no one rescuing them; plunder, with no one saying, “Give it back!”
Who among you will heed this, receive [it], and consider the outcome?

Who handed Jacob over to spoil and Israel to plunderers? Was it not יְיָ, because they sinned before Him, would not walk in the ways that are proper before Him, and did not receive the instruction of His Torah?

He poured out upon them the fury of His anger, and brought against them the might of His warriors. They killed among them on every side, yet they did not know; they ruled over them, yet they did not lay His fear upon their heart.’

qualifications.he: הלוחמים הם ההורגים והשולטים; העם שנפגע הוא שלא הבין ולא שם את יראתו על לב. כינויי הגוף מתחלפים בין שתי הקבוצות.
qualifications.en: The warriors are those who kill and rule; the stricken people are those who did not understand and did not take His fear to heart. The pronouns shift between these two groups.

pairs.fullEnglish: For their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed blood.
For in vain is the net spread over the winged birds.

qualifications.he: הדימוי של הרשת והעופות נקשר למארב הפוגע בחיי האורבים בפסוקים יח–יט. אין כאן קביעה עצמאית שכל פרישת רשת חסרת תועלת.
qualifications.en: The image of the net and birds is connected to the ambush endangering the ambushers’ own lives in verses 18–19. It is not an independent claim that setting any net is useless.

pairs.fullEnglish: But they lie in wait for their own blood, and hide to ambush their own lives.
Such are the ways of all those who commit wrongdoing: they take away the lives of their possessors.

qualifications.he: כינוי השייכות נקשר כאן לבעלי הדרכים הרעות: חייהם שלהם ניטלים. זהו המשך האזהרה שבפסוק יח.
qualifications.en: The possessive is taken here to refer to those who follow the evil ways: their own lives are taken. This continues the warning in verse 18.

pairs.fullEnglish: Wisdom is praised in the marketplace, and gives her voice in the streets.
At the head of the fortified places she proclaims, and at the entrance of the gates in the towns she speaks her words:

qualifications.he: בִּירָתָא מתורגמת כאן כמקומות מבוצרים; משמעותו המדויקת של מונח המקום אינה מוכרעת.
qualifications.en: בִּירָתָא is rendered here as fortified places; the precise meaning of this location term is uncertain.

pairs.fullEnglish: And now thus said יְיָ, who created you, Jacob, and who established you, Israel: ‘Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have raised you by your name; you are Mine.

For at the first, when you crossed through the Sea of Reeds, My Word was your help. Pharaoh and the Egyptians, who were as numerous as the waters of a river, could not prevail over you. And also at the second, when you go among nations as powerful as fire, they will not prevail over you; and kingdoms as strong as a flame will not destroy you.

qualifications.he: התרגום מבחין בין מעבר ים סוף בעבר ובין הליכה עתידית בין אומות, ואינו מדבר רק על מים ואש כפשוטם.
qualifications.en: The Targum distinguishes the past crossing of the Sea of Reeds from a later passage among nations; it does not speak only of literal water and fire.

pairs.fullEnglish: For I am יְיָ, your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Redeemer. I gave the Egyptians in exchange for you, Cush and Seva in your place.
Because you are beloved before Me, you have been honored, and I have loved you; I have handed over nations in your place and kingdoms in exchange for your life.
Do not fear, for My Word is your help. From the east I will bring your children, and from the west I will bring your exiles near.’
‘How long will the inexperienced love inexperience, scoffers desire scoffing for themselves, and fools hate knowledge?
Turn toward my reproof; I will pour forth my spirit to you and make my words known to you.
Because I called and you did not believe, I raised my hand and you did not listen,

qualifications.he: פסוקים כד–כה מתארים את דחיית הקריאה והעצה; התוצאה מתחילה באף אני שבפסוק כו ונמשכת הלאה. אין זו הבטחה אוטומטית לכל אדם שנפל בצרה.
qualifications.en: Verses 24–25 describe the rejection of the call and counsel; the consequence begins with ‘I too’ in verse 26 and continues afterward. It is not an automatic statement about everyone who encounters trouble.

pairs.fullEnglish: and you set aside all my counsel and did not desire reproof—
I too will laugh at your downfall, and will mock when turmoil comes upon you.’

dayTitle.he: בריאת העולם, האור והציווי על הרקיע
dayTitle.en: Creation, light, and the command for an expanse

explanation.he: הקריאה נפתחת בבריאת השמים והארץ ובמצב הארץ והמים. אונקלוס מתאר רוח מלפני ה׳ הנושבת על פני המים. אחר כך באים האור, ההבדלה בינו ובין החושך ושמות היום והלילה, ובסיום נאמר הציווי על הרקיע.
explanation.en: The reading opens with the creation of heavens and earth and the condition of the earth and waters. Onkelos describes a wind from before יְיָ blowing over the waters. Light, its separation from darkness, and the naming of day and night follow; the passage ends with the command for an expanse.

dayTitle.he: עשיית הרקיע, קיבוץ המים וגילוי היבשה
dayTitle.en: The expanse, the gathering of water, and the appearance of dry land

explanation.he: כאן מתוארת עשיית הרקיע וההפרדה בין המים שמתחתיו למים שמעליו. לאחר קריאת שמו שמים בא הציווי לקבץ את המים ולגלות את היבשה. ליבשה ולקיבוץ המים ניתנים השמות ארץ וימים.
explanation.en: This passage describes making the expanse and separating the waters below it from those above it. After the expanse is named Heavens, the waters are commanded to gather and the dry land to appear. The dry land and the gathered waters receive the names Earth and Seas.

dayTitle.he: צמיחת הזרע והפרי והציווי על המאורות
dayTitle.en: Seed-bearing growth and the command concerning the lights

explanation.he: האדמה מצמיחה צמחים ועצי פרי למיניהם, והזרע נזכר כחלק מתיאור הצמיחה. בהמשך נאמר הציווי על המאורות שיבדילו בין היום ללילה ויהיו לאותות ולמועדים. בתרגום מודגש גם מניין הימים והשנים באמצעותם.
explanation.en: The earth brings forth plants and fruit trees according to their kinds, with seed included in the description of their growth. The command concerning lights then distinguishes day from night and gives them a role in signs and appointed times. Onkelos also explicitly speaks of counting days and years by them.

dayTitle.en: The lights, the creatures of the waters, and the birds

explanation.he: עשיית שני המאורות והכוכבים מתוארת עם תפקידיהם בהארה ובהבדלה בין אור לחושך. אחר כך נאמר שהמים ישרצו נפש חיה ושהעופות יעופו על פני הרקיע. התיאור כולל את בריאת התנינים הגדולים, יצורי המים והעוף למיניהם.
explanation.en: The making of the two lights and the stars is described together with their roles in illumination and the separation of light from darkness. The waters are then commanded to teem with living creatures, and birds to fly across the expanse of the heavens. The account includes the great sea creatures, the creatures moving in the waters, and birds according to their kinds.

dayTitle.he: ברכת בעלי החיים והאמירה על עשיית האדם
dayTitle.en: The blessing of the creatures and the declaration concerning humankind

explanation.he: ברכת הפרייה והריבוי ניתנת לבעלי החיים שבמים ולעופות. אחריה בא תיאור הוצאת בעלי החיים היבשתיים ועשייתם למיניהם. הקטע מסתיים באמירה ״נעשה אדם״ ובתיאור השלטון שניתן לו בבעלי החיים; עצם תיאור בריאת האדם בא בקריאה הבאה.
explanation.en: The blessing of fruitfulness and increase is given to the creatures of the waters and to birds. The account then turns to the bringing forth and making of land creatures according to their kinds. It ends with “Let Us make a human” and the declared rule over the creatures; the actual account of creating the human follows in the next reading.

dayTitle.he: בריאת האדם, השלמת המלאכה וגן עדן
dayTitle.en: Humankind, completed creation, and the Garden of Eden

explanation.he: הקריאה מתארת את בריאת האדם, ברכתו והמזון שניתן לו ולבעלי החיים, ואחר כך את השלמת המלאכה וקדושת היום השביעי. בהמשך באים יצירת האדם וגן עדן, הנהרות, הציווי על האכילה ובקשת הסעד לאדם. אונקלוס נוקט כאן לשון ״רוח ממללא״, והקריאה מסתיימת בהפלת השינה ולקיחת הצלע.
explanation.en: The reading describes the creation and blessing of humankind and the food given to humans and other creatures, followed by completed creation and the sanctification of the seventh day. It then turns to the formation of the human, the garden and its rivers, the command about eating, and the need for a corresponding support. Onkelos uses the expression “a speaking spirit”; the passage ends with sleep being cast upon the human and the taking of a rib.

dayTitle.he: מן המשפחה הראשונה אל הדורות שלפני המבול
dayTitle.en: From the first household to the generations before the flood

explanation.he: הקריאה עוברת מעשיית האשה אל הפרת הציווי והשילוח מן הגן, מעשה קין והבל ושושלות הדורות עד נח. בדברי ה׳ לקין נאמר בתרגום במפורש ששיפור המעשים ותשובה קשורים לסליחה. בסיום מתוארים ריבוי הרעה, ארכת מאה ועשרים השנים הקשורה לתשובה, ומציאת הרחמים לנח.
explanation.en: The reading moves from the making of the woman to the breach of the command, expulsion from the garden, the account of Cain and Hevel, and the generations leading to Noach. In the words to Cain, Onkelos explicitly connects improved deeds and repentance with forgiveness. The ending describes increasing wickedness, a reprieve of one hundred and twenty years linked to repentance, and Noach finding mercy.

dayTitle.en: The Light of Torah, Redemption, and New Praise

explanation.he: התרגום פותח בה׳, אלוהי העולם, שברא את השמים ותלה אותם, השלים את הארץ ויושביה ונותן נשמה ורוח לחיים בה. הוא מתאר גידול באמת, חיזוק והעמדה לשם ברית עם ואור עמים, ומפרש את פתיחת העיניים כפתיחת עיני בית ישראל הדומים לעיוורים ביחס לתורה, ואת הפדות כשחרור משעבוד מלכויות. המילה החריגה נַלְוַתְהוֹן שבסעיף ההוצאה מבין העמים מובנת מן ההקשר כגולים שלהם, אך קריאה זו נותרת מסופקת. בהמשך ה׳ אינו נותן לעם אחר את הכבוד שבו התגלה לישראל, ואינו נותן את שבחו לעובדי צלמים; ההודעה על חדשות בטרם בואן מובילה לקריאה לשבח חדש מקצות הארץ, מן הים ומן האיים ויושביהם.
explanation.en: The Targum opens with יְיָ, God of the world, who created and suspended the heavens, completed the earth and its inhabitants, and gives breath and spirit to those living upon it. It describes raising in truth, strengthening, and establishment for a covenant of a people and a light of nations, explaining the opening of eyes as opening those of the house of Israel, who are like the blind in relation to Torah, and redemption as release from subjection to kingdoms. The unusual word נַלְוַתְהוֹן in the clause about bringing people out from among the nations is understood from context as ‘their exiles,’ but that reading remains uncertain. יְיָ then withholds from another people the glory with which He revealed Himself to Israel, and withholds His praise from image-worshippers; the announcement of new things before their arrival leads to a call for new praise from the ends of the earth, the sea, and the islands and their inhabitants.

dayTitle.he: שבח היוצאים מבתי עולמם והתגלות הדין
dayTitle.en: Praise from the Dead Leaving Their Resting Places, and Revealed Judgment

explanation.he: לצד שבח המדבר ועריו, שמחת יושבי מדבר ערב והכרזת השבח באיים, התרגום מוסיף במפורש את המתים שישבחו בצאתם מבתי עולמם וירימו קול מראשי ההרים. הוא מתאר שוב ושוב את התגלות ה׳ לעשות גבורות, ובכלל זה התגלות ברוגז נגד אויביו. המילים מִלוּל וזִיעַ מובנות כאמירה ורעד, אך הקשר התחבירי שלהן להתגלות הגבורה אינו מוכרע. לבסוף ארכת הזמן מוסברת כהזדמנות לחזור לתורה שלא נוצלה, ולאחר שלא חזרו מתואר הדין המתגלה עליהם כחבלי יולדה, עם שממה וכליה יחד.
explanation.en: Alongside the praise of the wilderness and its towns, the rejoicing of those in the Arabian desert, and the declaration of praise in the islands, the Targum expressly adds the dead who will praise when they leave their eternal resting places and raise their voices from the mountaintops. It repeatedly describes יְיָ revealing Himself to perform mighty deeds, including revelation in anger against His enemies. The words מִלוּל and זִיעַ are understood as an utterance and trembling, but their syntactic relation to the revelation of might remains uncertain. Finally, the long reprieve is explained as an unused opportunity to return to Torah, and after their failure to return, the judgment revealed upon them is likened to birth pangs, with desolation and perishing together.

dayTitle.he: הדרכת בית ישראל והכינוי עבדים התלוי בתשובה
dayTitle.en: Guiding the House of Israel, and Being Called Servants upon Repentance

explanation.he: מול חורבן ההרים וייבוש הצמחייה והאגמים, התרגום מזהה את הדומים לעיוורים כבית ישראל: ה׳ יוליך אותם בדרכים שלא הכירו, יהפוך לפניהם חושך לאור ומקום קשה למישור ולא ירחיק אותם. לעומתם, עובדי הצלמים האומרים לפסל מתכת שהוא אלוהיהם ייסוגו לאחור וייבושו. הקריאה לשמוע ולראות מופנית במפורש לרשעים ולחייבים המדומים לחירשים ולעיוורים, ולא מוצגת כתיאור של ליקוי גופני בלבד. מול עונש החטאים, הכינוי עבדי ה׳ מותנה בתשובה; הקישור שבאנגלית בין החייבים שנשלחו אליהם נביאים ובין הכינוי עבדים הושלם בסוגריים, ואינו מפורש בארמית או ציווי חדש.
explanation.en: Against the devastation of mountains and the drying of vegetation and pools, the Targum identifies those like the blind as the house of Israel: יְיָ will lead them on unfamiliar ways, turn darkness before them into light and rough ground into a level place, and not cast them far away. By contrast, image-worshippers who call a cast image their gods will turn backward in shame. The call to hear and see explicitly addresses the wicked and guilty, compared to the deaf and blind, rather than presenting only a description of bodily impairment. Against the punishment of sins, being called the servants of יְיָ is conditional upon repentance; the English link between the guilty to whom prophets were sent and being called servants is supplied in brackets, not explicit in the Aramaic or a new imperative.

dayTitle.he: עושי התורה והעם שלא קיבל את הוראתה
dayTitle.en: Those Who Carry Out Torah and the People Who Rejected Its Instruction

explanation.he: התרגום פונה בלשון רבים למי שראו רבות אך לא שמרו, בלי לפרש את מושא השמירה, ושאוזניהם נפתחו אך לא קיבלו הוראה. מול זאת הוא מפרש שה׳ רוצה לזכות את ישראל, ושהוא יגדל ויחזק את עושי תורתו. תיאור העם הבזוז, הצעירים המכוסים בושה והמעונים בבתי מאסר מוביל לקריאה להתבונן בתוצאה, ולביאור שיעקב וישראל נמסרו לבוזזים מפני שחטאו, סירבו ללכת בדרכים הראויות לפני ה׳ ולא קיבלו את הוראת תורתו. בסיום הלוחמים שה׳ הביא הם ההורגים והשולטים, ואילו העם שנפגע הוא שלא הבין ולא שם את יראת ה׳ על לבו.
explanation.en: The Targum addresses in the plural those who saw many things but did not keep, without specifying the object of keeping, and whose ears were opened but who did not receive instruction. In contrast, it explains that יְיָ desires to grant Israel merit and will exalt and strengthen those who carry out His Torah. The account of a plundered people, young men covered with shame, and those afflicted in prisons leads to a call to consider the outcome, and to the explanation that Jacob and Israel were handed to plunderers because they sinned, refused the ways proper before יְיָ, and did not receive His Torah's instruction. At the close, the warriors whom יְיָ brought are those who kill and rule, while the stricken people are those who did not understand or take His fear to heart.

dayTitle.he: עזרת מימרו של ה׳: מים סוף ועד קירוב הגולים
dayTitle.en: The Help of God's Word: From the Sea of Reeds to Bringing Exiles Near

explanation.he: התרגום פותח בה׳ שברא את יעקב והעמיד את ישראל, גאל אותו וגידל אותו בשמו, ומתוך כך אומר לו שלא לפחד ושהוא שלו. הוא מבחין בין מעבר ים סוף בעבר, שבו מימרו של ה׳ היה לעזר ופרעה והמצרים הרבים כמי נהר לא יכלו לישראל, ובין הליכה עתידית בין אומות התקיפות כאש ומלכויות החזקות כשלהבת שלא יוכלו להם ולא ישמידו אותם. ה׳ מציג את עצמו כאלוהי ישראל, קדושו וגואלו, ומתאר את מסירת המצרים, כוש וסבא תחתיו ואת מסירת העמים והמלכויות תמורת חייו על רקע אהבתו וכבודו. בסיום חוזרת ההבטחה שמימרו של ה׳ הוא לעזר, ונאמר שיביא את בניו ממזרח ויקרב את גוליו ממערב.
explanation.en: The Targum opens with יְיָ, who created Jacob and established Israel, redeemed him and raised him by his name, and therefore tells him not to fear and that he belongs to Him. It distinguishes the past crossing of the Sea of Reeds, when God's Word was their help and Pharaoh and the Egyptians, numerous as river waters, could not prevail over Israel, from a later passage among nations powerful as fire and kingdoms strong as a flame that will neither prevail over them nor destroy them. יְיָ identifies Himself as Israel's God, Holy One, and Redeemer, describing the giving of the Egyptians, כּוּשׁ and סְבָא in Israel's place, and nations and kingdoms in exchange for Israel's life, in the setting of His love and the honor granted to Israel. The closing assurance again names God's Word as help and promises to bring Israel's children from the east and bring Israel's exiles near from the west.

explanation.he: פתיחת התרגום מציגה את לימוד המשלים כדרך לדעת חכמה ומוסר ולהבין אמרי בינה. קבלת המוסר קשורה בהשכלה, בצדקה, בדין וביושר, ולא בצבירת ידיעות בלבד. הפתאים מקבלים ערמה והצעירים דעת ומחשבה, ואילו החכם נקרא להוסיף דעת והנבון לקנות הנהגה. החתימה פונה להבנת משלים, דברי חכמים וחידותיהם, ומזכירה גם פִלְאֲתָא, המתורגמת כאן כאמרה מופלאה, אך יחסה המדויק לחידה או למליצה אינו מוכרע.
explanation.en: The opening of the Targum presents the study of proverbs as a way to know wisdom and discipline and to understand sayings of discernment. Receiving discipline is connected with understanding, righteousness, judgment, and uprightness, not merely with accumulating information. The inexperienced receive prudence and the young knowledge and thought, while the wise person is called to increase knowledge and the discerning person to acquire guidance. The closing turns to understanding proverbs, the words of the wise, and their riddles, and also mentions פִלְאֲתָא, rendered here as a wondrous saying, though its exact relation to a riddle or figurative saying is uncertain.

dayTitle.en: The Beginning of Wisdom and Listening to Parents

explanation.he: התרגום מגדיר את יראת ייָ כראשית החכמה, ומעמיד מולה את הכסילים המבזים חכמה ומוסר. הבן נקרא לשמוע את מוסר אביו ולא לסטות מהוראת אמו; שניהם מתוארים כיופי וחן לראשו וכענק לצווארו. מתוך ההקשבה הזאת באה האזהרה המפורשת שלא להתרצות לחוטאים אם יפתו אותו.
explanation.en: The Targum defines the fear of ייָ as the beginning of wisdom, in contrast to fools who scorn wisdom and discipline. The son is called to hear his father’s discipline and not to stray from his mother’s teaching; both are described as beauty and grace for his head and a necklace for his neck. Alongside this listening comes the explicit warning not to consent if sinners entice him.

dayTitle.en: Rejecting the Lure of Shared Plunder

explanation.he: הפתיחה המותנית של התרגום מציגה את דברי המפתים: הם מזמינים את הבן למארב לשפיכות דמים ולפגיעה בחפים מפשע ללא עילה. דימויי הבליעה בחיים כקבר והירידה לבור שייכים לאיומיהם כלפי הקרבנות, ואינם הוראה של האב. הבטחותיהם לעושר ולחפצים יקרים, לבתים מלאי שלל ולכיס אחד לכולם נמשכות עד סוף דברי הפיתוי. תשובת האב באה אחריהן כאזהרה לבנו שלא ללכת עמם ולמנוע את רגלו משביליהם.
explanation.en: The conditional opening of the Targum introduces the enticers’ words: they invite the son to an ambush for bloodshed and an attack on the innocent without cause. The images of swallowing people alive like the grave and going down to the pit belong to their threats against the victims, not to the father’s instruction. Their promises of wealth and precious things, houses filled with plunder, and one purse for everyone continue to the end of the enticement. The father’s response follows as a warning to his son not to go with them and to hold back his foot from their paths.

dayTitle.en: The Ambushers’ Own Peril and Wisdom’s Voice

explanation.he: התרגום מנמק את האזהרה מפני דרכי הרשעים בריצתם לרע ובחיפזונם לשפוך דם, וקושר את דימוי הרשת הפרושה על העופות למארב הפוגע באורבים עצמם, ולא לקביעה שכל רשת חסרת תועלת. האורבים מסכנים את דמם ואת חייהם שלהם, וגם האמירה על נטילת חיי בעלי הדרכים הרעות מובנת כאן כהמשך לאותה אזהרה. מכאן עובר הקטע לחכמה, המשובחת בשוק ומשמיעה את קולה ברחובות ואת דבריה בפתחי שערי הערים. מקום הכרזתה מתואר גם במילה בִּירָתָא, המתורגמת כאן כמקומות מבוצרים, אך משמעותו המדויקת של מונח המקום אינה מוכרעת.
explanation.en: The Targum grounds the warning against the evildoers’ ways in their rush toward evil and their haste to shed blood, linking the image of the net spread over birds to the ambush that endangers the ambushers themselves, not to a claim that every net is useless. The ambushers endanger their own blood and lives, and the statement about taking the lives of those who follow evil ways is understood here as continuing that warning. The passage then turns to Wisdom, who is praised in the marketplace and gives her voice in the streets and her words at the entrances of the town gates. The place of her proclamation is also described by בִּירָתָא, rendered here as fortified places, though the precise meaning of this location term is uncertain.

dayTitle.en: Wisdom’s Reproof and the Cost of Rejecting It

explanation.he: החכמה מדברת בתרגום אל הפתאים האוהבים פתיות, אל הלצים החפצים בלצון ואל הכסילים השונאים דעת. היא קוראת לפנות לתוכחתה ומבטיחה להביע להם את רוחה ולהודיע את דבריה; הרוח והדברים שייכים לחכמה הדוברת. אחר כך היא מתארת כיצד קראה ולא האמינו, הרימה את ידה ולא הקשיבו, וכיצד דחו את כל עצתה ולא רצו בתוכחה. הצחוק על שברם והלעג בבוא המהומה מוצגים כתוצאה של דחייה זו, ולא כאמירה אוטומטית על כל אדם הנקלע לצרה.
explanation.en: In the Targum, Wisdom addresses the inexperienced who love inexperience, the scoffers who desire scoffing, and the fools who hate knowledge. She calls them to turn toward her reproof and promises to pour forth her spirit to them and make her words known; the spirit and words belong to Wisdom, who is speaking. She then describes how she called and they did not believe, raised her hand and they did not listen, and how they set aside all her counsel and did not desire reproof. Her laughter at their downfall and mockery when turmoil comes are presented as the consequence of this rejection, not as an automatic statement about everyone who encounters trouble.
